landmarks.name: Mercedes-Benz Stadium
landmarks.look: Pinwheel retractable roof of eight translucent petals over a white-and-grey steel bowl; sits low at the edge of the Downtown grid with a glass-walled concourse.

landmarks.name: State Farm Arena
landmarks.look: Squat, rounded arena block of pale stone and dark glass beside the stadium, with a wide plaza and a tall sign band on the south face.

landmarks.name: Georgia World Congress Center
landmarks.look: A long, low convention complex of beige precast and glass halls with covered walkways over Andrew Young International Boulevard.

landmarks.name: The Center
landmarks.look: Multi-tower complex of concrete and glass around a tall open atrium over the Techwood/Marietta streets; now called The Center, with its office towers being converted to a hotel and apartments.
landmarks.note: Not verified. No Wikipedia coordinates found. OSM way 41439893 ("The CTR", the Center complex) sits at 33.757606,-84.394920, 234 m from the current point. Overpass was unavailable, so this is from Nominatim only.

landmarks.name: Centennial Olympic Park
landmarks.look: Open lawns, a long reflecting pool and fountain plaza, and tall palm and flag lines, bounded by the stadium and the CNN block.

landmarks.name: Fountain of Rings
landmarks.look: A large circular water feature of interlocking rings and jets in the middle of the park's central plaza, with a low stone rim.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM fountain way 40697210 is at 33.759496,-84.392887, 135 m from the current point. Wikipedia gives only the park centroid (33.760042,-84.393229), so no second point for the fountain itself.

landmarks.name: SkyView Atlanta
landmarks.look: A tall white observation wheel of enclosed glass gondolas on a steel frame, standing at the edge of the park near the aquarium.

landmarks.name: Georgia Aquarium
landmarks.look: Large, blocky aquarium building of grey and green glass and stone with a wide plaza entrance off Baker Street.

landmarks.name: World of Coca-Cola
landmarks.look: Modern museum block of red-and-white panels and glass, with a tall soda-bottle-shaped sign and a plaza with pedestrian crossing.

landmarks.name: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
landmarks.displayName: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
landmarks.look: Low, modern museum of glass and pale stone set around a plaza, with a neutral, reflective facade and a long wall of inscribed panels along the street.

landmarks.name: College Football Hall of Fame
landmarks.look: Tall, glassy museum block of red-brick and glass near the park, with a sculptural stadium-like frame at the entrance.

landmarks.name: Georgia State Capitol
landmarks.look: Granite-and-marble Classical capitol on a hill, with a tall gilded dome and a long flight of steps and a lawn facing Washington Street.
landmarks.note: Main portico faces west onto Washington Street; the rear (east) facade faces Capitol Avenue. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_State_Capitol ("The Capitol faces west on Washington Street"), corroborated by the NPS description of Capitol Square (https://www.nps.gov/nr/travel/Atlanta/geo.htm).

landmarks.name: Atlanta City Hall
landmarks.look: Stone-clad Art Deco-style civic building with a tall stepped tower and a flat plaza on Trinity Avenue.

landmarks.name: Westin Peachtree Plaza
landmarks.look: Tall cylindrical hotel tower with a flat top and an exterior glass elevator tube running up one side of the concrete shell.

landmarks.name: Hyatt Regency Atlanta
landmarks.look: Hotel with a large blue-tinted glass dome, a flat tower block and a long atrium, near Peachtree Center.

landmarks.name: Atlanta Marriott Marquis
landmarks.look: Tall tower of tinted glass and white-grey panels with a stepped top, rising from a wide Peachtree Center podium.

landmarks.name: Truist Plaza
landmarks.look: Tall office tower of blue-green glass with a stepped crown and a rounded top, in the Peachtree Center skyline.

landmarks.name: 191 Peachtree Tower
landmarks.look: Slender glass office tower with a crowned top and a stepped setback at the upper floors, rising from a plaza on Peachtree Street.

landmarks.name: Georgia-Pacific Tower
landmarks.look: Tall, grey-glass office tower with a flat top and a regular window grid, on the Peachtree Street spine of Downtown.

landmarks.name: Flatiron Building
landmarks.look: A narrow, triangular red-brick and stone building of a few storeys sitting on the wedge at Five Points, with a pointed prow.

landmarks.name: Candler Building
landmarks.look: A tall Beaux-Arts style office building of terracotta and stone with a decorated top and a long ornamental cornice.

landmarks.name: Five Points station
landmarks.look: Underground transit hub with a glass-and-steel entrance pavilion and wide plaza at the Five Points intersection.

landmarks.name: Underground Atlanta
landmarks.look: Entertainment district of shops and restaurants in the streets below street level, with brick arcades and a tall clock tower over the entrance.

landmarks.name: Woodruff Park
landmarks.look: Small urban park of mature trees, benches and paved walks, with a plaza and a fountain amid the towers of Peachtree Center.

landmarks.name: Rialto Center for the Arts
landmarks.look: A former movie palace with a tall, decorated brick and terracotta facade and a marquee sign on Forsyth Street.

landmarks.name: Sweet Auburn Curb Market
landmarks.look: Long, low brick market hall with a metal-roofed arcade and a lively row of food stalls along Edgewood Avenue.

landmarks.name: Georgia State University Student Center
landmarks.look: Modern campus building of brick and glass with a wide stair and plaza facing the downtown campus green.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Only the campus-level Wikipedia point (33.753694,-84.385972) exists, and no OSM building was found.

landmarks.name: Georgia State University Library
landmarks.look: Tall, plain institutional library block of tinted glass and concrete on the Downtown campus.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Only the campus-level Wikipedia point (33.753694,-84.385972) exists, and no OSM building was found.

landmarks.name: The Gulch
landmarks.look: A low, historically rail-cut area of concrete viaduct and new mixed-use construction between Downtown and the Westside.
landmarks.note: Not verified. No coordinates or OSM element found.

landmarks.name: Centennial Yards
landmarks.look: A large, mostly open rail yard being redeveloped with towers, plazas and a stadium-side district on the Gulch rail corridor.

landmarks.name: Peachtree Center station
landmarks.look: Transit station entrance under the Peachtree Center plaza, between tall hotels and offices.

landmarks.name: Fulton County Courthouse
landmarks.look: Massive stone Classical courthouse with columns and a wide set of steps, at the west edge of Downtown.

landmarks.name: Central Library (Atlanta-Fulton Public Library)
landmarks.look: Large, glassy library of stepped, angled glass planes and a faceted stone plinth at Margaret Mitchell Square.

landmarks.name: Ebenezer Baptist Church
landmarks.look: Modest brick church with a plain front and a tall steeple, on Auburn Avenue in the Sweet Auburn historic district.

landmarks.name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historic Site
landmarks.displayName: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historic Site
landmarks.look: A cluster of restored early-20th-century houses and a visitor center on Auburn Avenue, kept quiet and simple, with a park-like setting.

landmarks.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Center for Nonviolent Social Change
landmarks.displayName: Martin Luther King Jr. Center for Nonviolent Social Change
landmarks.look: A reflecting pool and a low stone tomb in a quiet plaza with a long, low museum and archive building beside it.

landmarks.name: Freedom Park
landmarks.look: Long linear park of lawns and tree rows along a former rail corridor, with the BeltLine trail running through it.

landmarks.name: Krog Street Tunnel
landmarks.look: A short brick and concrete railway tunnel under Krog Street, its inside and portals covered in dense, colourful murals and graffiti.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Wikipedia and Wikidata both give 33.7528,-84.3636 (33°45′10″N 84°21′49″W), 799 m from the current point. No OSM tunnel element found; that Wikipedia point is on Krog Street SE (OSM way 44062162). Coordinates left unchanged until an OSM check confirms the point.

landmarks.name: Ponce City Market
landmarks.look: Huge former mail-order warehouse of red brick and tall steel-sash windows, with a big clock tower and a rooftop Ferris wheel.

landmarks.name: Krog Street Market
landmarks.look: Brick and steel food hall in a converted old warehouse, with a lot of graffiti and mural art on the exterior.

landmarks.name: Lake Claire Community Land Trust
landmarks.look: A tree-lined residential neighborhood of bungalows and small cottages around a small lake, with a community centre and shared lots.

landmarks.name: Edgewood Shopping Center
landmarks.look: Low, long strip of one-storey shopfronts with a shared parking lot along Edgewood Avenue.
landmarks.note: Not verified. No coordinates or OSM element found.

landmarks.name: Old Fourth Ward Park
landmarks.look: A large park of lawns, a long reflecting pool, a play area and a steep grassy slope on the BeltLine, next to the towers of Ponce.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Wikipedia gives Historic Fourth Ward Park at 33.7553,-84.3726, 598 m from the current point. Only one source; no OSM element checked.

landmarks.name: Little Five Points
landmarks.look: A small, crowded crossroads of brick storefronts, shops and bars, with a painted mural and a steady street scene.

landmarks.name: Candler Park
landmarks.look: A leafy neighborhood park of large oaks, open lawns and a small lake, bounded by bungalows.

landmarks.name: Inman Park
landmarks.look: A historic streetcar suburb of Victorian houses, big porches and tree-lined streets under mature oaks.

landmarks.name: Piedmont Park
landmarks.look: Big city park of open lawns, a lake, a long meadow and a sweeping tree canopy, with the Midtown towers on its east edge.

landmarks.name: Fox Theatre
landmarks.look: Ornate Moorish-revival theatre with a tall onion-domed roof and a long marquee sign on Peachtree Street.

landmarks.name: The Varsity
landmarks.look: A drive-in restaurant with a bright red-and-white sign tower and a large parking lot with car hops.

landmarks.name: Bank of America Plaza
landmarks.look: Tall, grey-glass office tower with a stepped and tapered crown, the tallest tower in the state.

landmarks.name: One Atlantic Center
landmarks.look: Tall, angular office tower with a stepped crown and a dark glass curtain wall.

landmarks.name: Atlanta Symphony Hall
landmarks.look: Concert hall of light stone and glass with a tall, flat-topped front, part of the Woodruff Arts Center campus.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Wikidata gives 33.7905,-84.3852, 162 m from the current point. OSM node 4541379516 (Atlanta Symphony Orchestra, Peachtree St NE) is at 33.788870,-84.385432, 86 m away. The sources do not agree.

landmarks.name: Tech Tower
landmarks.look: Small, collegiate Gothic-style tower of stone with a tall spire, on the Georgia Tech campus.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM way 28951319 ("Tech Tower") is at 33.772370,-84.394698, 316 m from the current point. No Wikipedia point to confirm.

landmarks.name: Atlanta Botanical Garden
landmarks.look: Garden of landscaped beds, a tall glass conservatory and a wide lawn beside Piedmont Park.

landmarks.name: Atlanta History Center
landmarks.look: Museum campus of low brick buildings and a historic house set among wooded grounds and gardens.

landmarks.name: Georgia Governor's Mansion
landmarks.look: Large white Classical residence behind a wall and a wooded lawn on West Paces Ferry Road.

landmarks.name: Lenox Square
landmarks.look: Large enclosed mall of pale stone and glass with a multi-level car park and a wide courtyard entrance on Peachtree Road.

landmarks.name: Phipps Plaza
landmarks.look: Upscale mall of beige stone and tinted glass, with a long multi-storey façade on Peachtree Road.

landmarks.name: Cathedral of St. Philip
landmarks.look: Large Gothic-revival stone church with a tall tower and a broad front lawn on Peachtree Road.

landmarks.name: Chastain Park Amphitheatre
landmarks.look: Open-air concert bowl of stone seating among tall pines in a wooded city park.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Wikipedia gives only the whole park (33.876772,-84.396157), 1.9 km from the current point, and no amphitheatre point.

landmarks.name: Vinings Village
landmarks.look: A small village centre of brick and frame shopfronts and cafes on a hill over the river, along Paces Ferry Road.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Wikipedia gives only the town centre (33.866361,-84.466069), 1.5 km from the current point. No village-specific point found.

landmarks.name: Cobb Galleria Centre
landmarks.look: Large convention and performing arts centre of glass and pale stone around a tall glazed atrium, next to the Galleria shopping district.

landmarks.name: Truist Park
landmarks.look: Baseball ballpark of brick, steel and open seating, with a long grand entry plaza and a large scoreboard at the outfield.

landmarks.name: The Battery Atlanta
landmarks.look: Outdoor mixed-use district of modern brick and glass buildings and open plazas around the ballpark.

landmarks.name: Spaghetti Junction
landmarks.look: Multi-level highway interchange of tall concrete ramps and curving overpasses where I-85 meets I-285.
landmarks.note: Not verified. The Wikipedia article redirects to Tom Moreland Interchange, which has no coordinates in the data retrieved. No OSM interchange element matched.

landmarks.name: Cobb Cloverleaf
landmarks.look: Wide, looping cloverleaf interchange of concrete ramps and high bridges where I-75 crosses I-285.
landmarks.note: Not verified. No Wikipedia point or OSM element found for this interchange.

landmarks.name: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport
landmarks.look: Large airport of long concourses, a tall glass control tower and runways, with long rows of parked aircraft on the apron.

landmarks.name: Domestic Terminal
landmarks.look: The long terminal of the North and South Terminals round a great glass-roofed atrium: ticketing, baggage claim, the security checkpoint, the rail station at its west end and the curbs under deep canopies.

landmarks.name: Concourse T
landmarks.look: The concourse joined to the Domestic Terminal: a long two-storey hall of glass gate lounges over the ramp level, with jet bridges.

landmarks.name: Concourse A
landmarks.look: A long, low two-storey concourse in the middle of the field, glazed gate lounges over the ramp level, a skylit spine and jet bridges down both sides.

landmarks.name: Concourse B
landmarks.look: A long, low two-storey concourse in the middle of the field, glazed gate lounges over the ramp level, a skylit spine and jet bridges down both sides.

landmarks.name: Concourse C
landmarks.look: A long, low two-storey concourse in the middle of the field, glazed gate lounges over the ramp level, a skylit spine and jet bridges down both sides.

landmarks.name: Concourse D
landmarks.look: The narrow concourse of the regional jets: a long two-storey hall with closely spaced jet bridges.

landmarks.name: Concourse E
landmarks.look: The international concourse built for the 1996 Games: taller, with widebody gates and jet bridges.

landmarks.name: Concourse F
landmarks.look: The international concourse of 2012: a curved roof with deep overhangs over a tall glass wall, widebody gates.

landmarks.name: Maynard H. Jackson Jr. International Terminal
landmarks.displayName: Maynard H. Jackson Jr. International Terminal
landmarks.look: The international terminal on the east side of the field: a long glass hall under a sweeping wing of a roof cantilevered over its curb.

landmarks.name: Atlanta Tower
landmarks.look: The 121 m (398 ft) air traffic control tower, the tallest in North America when it opened: a slender concrete shaft and a wide cab of outward-leaning dark glass.

landmarks.name: North Hourly Parking
landmarks.look: A four-level concrete parking deck by the North Terminal curb.

landmarks.name: North Daily Parking
landmarks.look: A four-level concrete parking deck north of the terminal.

landmarks.name: South Hourly Parking
landmarks.look: A four-level concrete parking deck by the South Terminal curb.

landmarks.name: South Daily Parking
landmarks.look: A four-level concrete parking deck south of the terminal.

landmarks.name: ATL West Parking Deck
landmarks.look: A seven-level parking deck by the Gateway Center on the SkyTrain.

landmarks.name: Rental Car Center
landmarks.look: Two four-level decks of rental cars with brick stair towers, a customer service hall and the SkyTrain station.

landmarks.name: ATL SkyTrain
landmarks.look: The elevated automated people mover from the Domestic Terminal to the Gateway Center and the Rental Car Center, a concrete guideway on single columns.

landmarks.name: Stone Mountain Park
landmarks.look: A huge granite dome rising from wooded parkland, with a long walk-up trail to the top and a lawn for a laser show.

landmarks.name: Stone Mountain carving
landmarks.look: A large carved relief high on the granite face of the mountain, shown as a distant, neutral landmark with no detail beyond its silhouette.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Wikipedia gives the mountain at 33.805944,-84.145422 and says the carving is on the north face, about 120 m up, but publishes no carving point. The current point is not confirmed.

landmarks.name: Lake Lanier
landmarks.look: A large reservoir of wooded shoreline, coves and marinas with a concrete dam at one end, handled quietly and without gags.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM relation 113346 is the lake, and its centre (about 34.29 N, 83.9 W) is a bounding-box centre rather than a usable point. No Wikipedia point found. The current point is kept as a rough anchor.

landmarks.name: Kennesaw Mountain
landmarks.look: A wooded ridge with rocky summits and walking trails, marked as a national battlefield park.

landmarks.name: Big Chicken
landmarks.look: Tall steel-framed roadside sign of a giant chicken on a lean post beside a busy arterial road.
landmarks.note: Position is the KFC building on Cobb Parkway that the sign stands beside (OSM way 197885182); Wikipedia gives 33.9514,-84.5204.

landmarks.name: Marietta Square
landmarks.look: A historic courthouse square of two-storey brick storefronts and a tall clock-topped courthouse in the middle.

landmarks.name: Six Flags Over Georgia
landmarks.look: Theme park of roller coasters and tall steel rides with a wide entry plaza and a large parking field.

landmarks.name: Mall of Georgia
landmarks.look: Large enclosed mall with a long grey-and-white facade and a wide surface car park.

landmarks.name: Decatur Square
landmarks.look: A small town square with a historic courthouse and brick two-storey shopfronts and cafes around it.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM way 25559294 (Decatur History Center, the old courthouse on East Court Square) is at 33.775129,-84.296514, 42 m from the current point. Wikipedia's Decatur point (33.7714,-84.2978) is the city centre, not the square.

landmarks.name: DeKalb-Peachtree Airport
landmarks.look: A small general-aviation airfield with a low terminal, hangars and a short runway among suburban trees.

landmarks.name: Atlanta Public Safety Training Center
landmarks.look: A training campus of low classroom buildings and a practice area in wooded land, built with a neutral, low-key design.

landmarks.name: Oakland Cemetery
landmarks.look: A historic Victorian cemetery of old stone monuments, tall oaks and winding paths, kept quiet and respectful.

landmarks.name: Zoo Atlanta
landmarks.look: A zoo in a hilly wooded park, with animal enclosures, paths and a tall entry gate.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM way 28798590 (zoo area centroid) is at 33.732598,-84.371038. Wikipedia and Wikidata give 33.73248,-84.36967, 127 m from the OSM centroid, so the sources disagree. The current point is 133 m from OSM.

landmarks.name: Grady Memorial Hospital
landmarks.look: Large hospital complex of tall brick and glass wings with a wide emergency entrance on Jesse Hill Jr. Drive.

landmarks.name: Concourse at Landmark Center (King and Queen towers)
landmarks.look: Two tall office towers of glass and stone, the taller one with a crown, standing side by side on a shared plaza by the highway.
landmarks.note: Not verified. Wikipedia's Concourse at Landmark Center gives 33.916,-84.355 (rounded), 1.3 km from the current point. No OSM element found.

landmarks.name: Atlanta Amtrak station
landmarks.look: A low station building of brick and steel with a canopy over the platform.
landmarks.note: Not verified. No coordinates found on Wikipedia or in the OSM lookups.

landmarks.name: Atlantic Station
landmarks.look: Mixed-use district of brick and glass towers and apartments built on a former steel mill site, with a long street grid and a central plaza.

landmarks.name: Atlanta BeltLine Eastside Trail
landmarks.look: A wide paved trail on an old rail corridor, with wooden footbridges, brick walls and new apartments along its length.

landmarks.name: Atlanta BeltLine Westside Trail
landmarks.look: A paved trail along a rail corridor through a former industrial area, with old brick buildings and newly built warehouses beside it.

landmarks.name: Atlanta BeltLine Southside Trail
landmarks.look: A paved trail through a wooded rail corridor past old cottages and small industrial buildings toward Grant Park.

landmarks.name: State of Georgia Building
landmarks.look: Tall 1960s office tower on Peachtree Street with a stepped crown.

landmarks.name: Hurt Building
landmarks.look: Wedge-shaped cream terra-cotta office building at Hurt Park, with a marble colonnade and a cornice.

landmarks.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
landmarks.displayName: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
landmarks.look: Red-brick Romanesque-Gothic basilica with twin spires.

landmarks.name: Corey Tower
landmarks.look: A slim round residential tower of Georgia State University.

landmarks.name: Peachtree Center Harris Tower
landmarks.look: A 31-storey slab of pale precast and ribbon windows with deep vertical piers, one of the Peachtree Center towers linked by skybridges.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM building way 536693776 is at 33.760754,-84.386460, 0 m from the current point. Wikipedia and Wikidata give no tower-specific coordinates to confirm.

landmarks.name: Peachtree Center International Tower
landmarks.look: A 30-storey slab in dark bronze glass and brown stone with a flat crown, linked to its neighbours by skybridges.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM building way 536691261 is at 33.759921,-84.386478, 1 m from the current point. Wikipedia gives no tower-specific coordinates. A separate OSM way 40808009 also named International Tower is at 33.761211,-84.387273.

landmarks.name: Peachtree Center North Tower
landmarks.look: A long 27-storey slab of warm grey precast with ribbon windows and vertical piers, linked by skybridges.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM building way 536690079 is at 33.760529,-84.387054, 0 m from the current point. Wikipedia gives no tower-specific coordinates to confirm.

landmarks.name: Peachtree Center South Tower
landmarks.look: A long 27-storey slab of warm grey precast with ribbon windows and vertical piers, twin to the North Tower and linked by skybridges.
landmarks.note: Not verified. OSM building way 536690082 is at 33.760166,-84.387060, 1 m from the current point. Wikipedia gives no tower-specific coordinates to confirm.

landmarks.name: Hilton Atlanta
landmarks.look: Wide 1971 hotel tower with a concave profile and a flat crown.
